report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of gated_writes.py: TaskSpec construction, relay gate composition, attempt runner, phase-1 gating, promotion lock. Claims checked; no critical issues found.
risks: gated_writes.py:281-339 | medium | TaskSpec metadata and gate_argv handling: gate_argv is built from gate dict, but _curated_relay_gate is only used when spec.gate_argv is truthy; if gate_argv is empty but gate_cwd/timeout set, the curated gate is ignored (matches docstring but could surprise callers). | Confirm intended behavior for gates with empty argv but non-empty cwd/timeout.

gated_writes.py:281-339 | medium | _spec_for docstring claims 'no task that lacks one sees its digest move' but this chunk cannot verify TaskSpec.body() behavior; relies on external module. | Inspect daedalus/spine/attempt.py TaskSpec.body().

gated_writes.py:341-371 | low | _curated_relay_gate docstring says both verdicts returned unchanged, but the curated gate result is the return of command_gate (not wrapped) and relay result is returned as-is when it fails; however, when relay passes, command_gate's result is returned directly. The claim is kept but the composition may not preserve the relay's gate output if relay passes and command_gate fails? Actually it returns command_gate's result, which is unchanged. No issue.

gated_writes.py:397-420 | medium | gate_candidates docstring says 'Never touches the primary checkout' but _attempt_assignment calls _recording_runner and run_attempt with repo_root=str(primary_root); this chunk cannot verify whether run_attempt touches primary checkout. | Inspect run_attempt and _recording_runner.

gated_writes.py:373-420 | low | gate_candidates docstring says returns in assignments order; code preserves order via results list and futs mapping, but ThreadPoolExecutor completion order doesn't matter. Kept.

gated_writes.py:422-470 | medium | _PromotionLock docstring claims same primitives as _BudgetLock and _RoomLock; this chunk cannot verify those external modules. | Inspect daedalus/budget.py and runs/council/room.py.

gated_writes.py:422-470 | medium | _PromotionLock __enter__ loop: if _acquire raises OSError, it retries until deadline; but if _acquire succeeds, it returns self. If file open fails, raises PromotionUnavailable. No issue. However, if _acquire raises a non-OSError exception (e.g., ValueError from msvcrt.locking), it propagates and the lock file is left open. Docstring says 'An unobtainable lock RAISES; it never silently proceeds unserialised.' This is true, but resource cleanup on unexpected exception is not handled. | Consider adding try/except around _acquire to close _fh on unexpected exceptions.

symbols.name: _spec_for
symbols.note: Builds a TaskSpec for an assignment with optional gate and model metadata. Uses rebase_declared_paths and uuid nonce. Adds rewrite_windows and model to metadata.

symbols.name: _curated_relay_gate
symbols.note: Composes _relay_gate and command_gate in order. Returns a gate function that first runs relay gate, then if passed runs command_gate with spec's gate args.

symbols.name: _attempt_assignment
symbols.note: Runs a single assignment through run_attempt using _recording_runner and _curated_relay_gate or _relay_gate. Returns a GatedCandidate.

symbols.name: _rev_parse_head
symbols.note: Runs 'git rev-parse --verify HEAD' in repo_root with timeout and hardened env. Raises RuntimeError on failure, returns trimmed stdout.

symbols.name: gate_candidates
symbols.note: Phase 1: runs all assignments concurrently via ThreadPoolExecutor, preserving order. Resolves ledger path and base commit if not provided. Loads model assignments from primary checkout.

symbols.name: PromotionUnavailable
symbols.note: RuntimeError subclass raised when promotion lock cannot be taken.

symbols.name: _PromotionLock
symbols.note: Cross-process lock using msvcrt on Windows, fcntl on POSIX. Fail-closed: raises PromotionUnavailable if lock cannot be acquired within timeout.

symbols.name: _PromotionLock.__init__
symbols.note: Initializes path, timeout_s, and _fh to None.

symbols.name: _PromotionLock.__enter__
symbols.note: Creates parent dir, opens lock file, retries _acquire until timeout, raises PromotionUnavailable on failure or timeout.

symbols.name: _PromotionLock._acquire
symbols.note: Attempts non-blocking lock: msvcrt.locking on Windows, fcntl.flock on POSIX.

symbols.name: _PromotionLock.__exit__
symbols.note: Unlocks and closes the file handle if present. Returns False always.

claims.text: None/empty reproduces the previous behaviour byte-for-byte, including the effect-key digest: TaskSpec.body() admits gate into the canonical body only when gate_argv is non-empty, so no task that lacks one sees its digest move.
claims.why: The claim about TaskSpec.body() and digest behavior is in daedalus.spine.attempt, not in this chunk. This chunk only shows gate_argv being set to empty tuple when gate is None/empty, which is consistent but not verifiable here.

claims.text: The argv is repo-authored, not model-authored: spine/picker.py builds it (docref's is sys.executable -m daedalus.spine.docref_gate ...), and the work-queue source validates it as a NUL-free string array out of a repo-curated file.
claims.why: References to spine/picker.py and work-queue source are outside this chunk. No code here verifies the provenance or validation.

claims.text: It is then executed by spine.attempt.command_gate as an argv list with no shell, at LOW INTEGRITY inside containment, in a Job Object, in the candidate's own worktree -- the same instrument, with the same containment, that already runs every default pytest gate.
claims.why: Execution details are in daedalus.spine.attempt.command_gate and containment layers, not in this chunk.

claims.text: A model-written patch cannot reach this path without a human git merge first, because the picker reads the primary checkout and promotion stops at an integration branch.
claims.why: Picker and promotion branch logic are outside this chunk.

claims.text: This makes 'window requested or silently lost?' answerable from one ledger row.
claims.why: Ledger row behavior is not in this chunk; only metadata dict includes rewrite_windows.

claims.text: THIS COMPOSITION IS THE WHOLE POINT, and it exists because putting gate_argv on the TaskSpec alone would have done NOTHING: TaskAttempt.__init__ gives an explicitly-passed gate= precedence over task.gate_argv, and this module always passes one.
claims.why: TaskAttempt.__init__ behavior is in daedalus.spine.attempt, not in this chunk. However, this module does always pass a gate via _attempt_assignment (either _curated_relay_gate or _relay_gate).

claims.text: Order matters ... 1. _relay_gate first, as a PRECONDITION. It is the only check that catches offload() finishing escalated_after_verify_fail with a NON-EMPTY wrote -- a write it could not fully roll back, kept visible on purpose.
claims.why: The behavior of offload() and _relay_gate is not in this chunk. The composition order is visible: relay first, then command_gate, so the claim about order is kept, but the specific reason about offload() is uncheckable.

claims.text: Both verdicts are returned UNCHANGED (never re-wrapped into a fresh GateResult), so containment attestations and gate output survive whichever one decides.
claims.why: In the code, first is returned directly if not passed, and command_gate(...)(ctx) is returned directly. No wrapping is visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Fail-closed: both must pass.
claims.why: The gate function returns first if it fails, otherwise returns command_gate result. Both must pass for the gate to pass.

claims.text: PHASE 1: run every write Assignment through TaskAttempt, concurrently.
claims.why: Uses ThreadPoolExecutor to submit _attempt_assignment for each assignment, which calls run_attempt (TaskAttempt).

claims.text: Returns one GatedCandidate per assignment, in assignments order (not completion order).
claims.why: results list is indexed by assignment order, and each future result is placed at its original index.

claims.text: Never touches the primary checkout -- see module docstring.
claims.why: This chunk does not show whether run_attempt or _recording_runner touches the primary checkout. However, gate_candidates itself only resolves the primary checkout for model assignments and does not modify it.

claims.text: cancel, when given, is forwarded to every TaskAttempt unchanged -- daedalus.spine.attempt._as_predicate normalises it (a bare callable, or anything exposing is_set(), both work with no adapter here).
claims.why: Normalization is in daedalus.spine.attempt._as_predicate, not in this chunk. The forwarding is visible: cancel is passed to _attempt_assignment and then to run_attempt.

claims.text: None (the default) reproduces today's behaviour exactly: no attempt in this batch is cooperatively cancellable.
claims.why: Whether attempts are cancellable depends on run_attempt and the gate function; not verifiable here. However, cancel=None is passed unchanged.

claims.text: This is deliberately request-scoped, not a module-level killswitch lookup -- a caller (e.g. a loop driver) that wants every attempt in one batch to share one cancel token passes it once, here; this module does not reach for global cancellation state on its own.
claims.why: No global state is visible in this chunk, but the claim about other modules is not verifiable.

claims.text: artifact_dir is optional for direct callers. run_write_wave always supplies the checkout-external content-addressed archive because it returns dictionaries rather than the live GatedCandidate objects.
claims.why: run_write_wave is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The isolated worktree is cut from committed HEAD and therefore (correctly) excludes dirty policy edits; letting offload rediscover the assignment there silently changed Lucia's measured 14B run back to the .env default.
claims.why: Offload and worktree behavior is outside this chunk. This chunk only shows that model assignments are resolved against the primary checkout.

claims.text: Same primitives as daedalus.budget._BudgetLock and runs/council/room.py's _RoomLock (msvcrt on Windows, fcntl on POSIX), independently written here -- both of those are private to modules this file does not own.
claims.why: The other lock implementations are not in this chunk. The primitives used here are indeed msvcrt and fcntl.

claims.text: Same fail-closed posture as the budget lock, and for the same reason: two promotions racing into one integration worktree is exactly the shared-mutable-state hazard this whole module exists to close, just moved one layer up.
claims.why: The budget lock's posture is not verifiable here. This lock does raise on failure, which is fail-closed.

claims.text: An unobtainable lock RAISES; it never silently proceeds unserialised.
claims.why: In __enter__, if _acquire fails after timeout, it raises PromotionUnavailable. If open fails, it also raises. It never returns None or proceeds without lock.

observations.what: _spec_for sets gate_argv from gate dict, but if gate_argv is empty, _attempt_assignment uses _relay_gate only, ignoring gate_cwd and timeout_s. This matches the docstring but could cause a gate with only cwd/timeout to be silently ignored.

_PromotionLock.__enter__ retries _acquire on OSError, but if _acquire raises a non-OSError (e.g., ValueError from msvcrt.locking), the exception propagates and _fh is left open. This could leak a file descriptor and leave the lock file locked.
gate_candidates resolves model assignments against primary checkout with a broad except Exception, failing to provider default. This is deliberate but could mask configuration errors.
_rev_parse_head uses subprocess.run with shell=False (default), which is safe. It uses _hardened_env() which is not shown here.
